**Question:** When deciding whether an address is a duplicate, how aggressively should the app treat near-identical addresses as "the same page"?

**Why it matters:** This sets when saving re-opens an existing bookmark versus creating a new one — too loose merges genuinely different pages, too strict lets duplicates slip in. It also defines the acceptance test for SC-004 (zero duplicates).

|--------|-------------|

| C | Aggressive — also drop all query parameters and `#fragments`, so only host + path matter |

**Question:** When deciding whether an address is a duplicate, how aggressively should the app treat near-identical addresses as "the same page"?

**Why it matters:** This sets when saving re-opens an existing bookmark versus creating a new one — too loose merges genuinely different pages, too strict lets duplicates slip in. It also defines the acceptance test for SC-004 (zero duplicates).

**Recommended:** Option B — matches how people expect duplicates to be caught (a trailing slash or `utm_` tracking tag shouldn't count as a new page) while keeping distinct paths and meaningful query parameters separate.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Exact match only — the address must be character-for-character identical |
| B | Normalize lightly — ignore scheme (http/https), a `www.` prefix, host capitalization, a trailing slash, and common tracking parameters (e.g. `utm_*`, `fbclid`); keep the path and other query parameters significant |
| C | Aggressive — also drop all query parameters and `#fragments`, so only host + path matter |
